titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 29: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 29. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲕⲑ] is printed with a bar above and below as the frame, not as a supralinear stroke. Measured strokes over ϥ of ⲧⲏⲣϥ (720–731), ⲛ of ⲛϩⲏⲧϥ (754–766), ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲟⲟⲩⲉ (859–873) and ⲛ of ϩⲛ (1158–1170).
Measured strokes over ϥ of ⲁϩϥ (646–658), over ϥ of ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲧϥ (863–875); the bar at 708–716 is the descender of ⲣ in l. 2.
Measured overline over ⲡⲛⲁ of ⲡⲉϥⲡⲛⲁ (727–772) covers ⲡ, ⲛ, ⲁ. Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (1081–1101): ⲙ 50 %, ⲛ 53 %, encoded on both. Strokes over ⲙ of ϩⲙ (641–654) and over ⲛ of ⲉⲧϩⲛ (1274–1287).

The bracket opened before the dot is closed after ⲧ; the dot is inside the restoration. The four dots at the line end stand without brackets. Measured stroke over ⲛⲛ of ⲛⲛⲕⲱⲧ (975–994): ⲛ 50 %, ⲛ 57 %, encoded on both. The stroke over ϩ of ⲛⲁⲣⲱⲭϩ is printed obliquely.
Four of the seven dots (x ≈ 596, 621, 648, 674) are faint (detector area ≤ 5, or above the ink threshold at x ≈ 674) but clear at 4× and by pixel values (minimum grey 129–137).
Line in ekthesis with an enlarged ⲛ inside the restoration.
Line in ekthesis with an enlarged ⲡ.
Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ of ⲁⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ (1083–1104): ⲙ 95 %, ⲛ 64 %, encoded on both.
A wide blank, not marked by the editors, stands before the enlarged ⲡ of ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ.
Measured stroke over ⲛⲛ of ⲛⲛⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ (711–730): ⲛ 50 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both.
Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (598–618): ⲙ 50 %, ⲛ 53 %, encoded on both. The stroke over ϩ of ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ is printed obliquely.
The stroke over ⲥ of ⲁϥϭⲗⲙⲗⲱⲙⲥ is printed obliquely. The third of the five dots (x ≈ 790) is faint (area 3) but clear at 4×. Measured stroke over ϩⲛ (967–987): ϩ 52 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both.
The edition prints an empty pair of brackets [ ] at the line start, then fourteen dots outside them.
A large middle dot (·) stands after ⲁⲧⲡⲉ, and an enlarged ⲉ begins ⲉϥⲙⲟⲩⲣ.

The edition prints ⲡ] at the line start with no opening bracket on this line or at the end of l. 27; the bracket is encoded as unpaired and ⲡ as read. The ϣ of ⲡⲉϥϣⲛⲉ has a separate sublinear dot in its lower bowl (6× zoom; the ϣ of ⲡⲉϥϣⲛⲉ in ll. 4, 19, 20 has none). Empty brackets [ ] stand between ⲡⲉ̣ and ⲉ.
An enlarged ⲡ begins ⲡⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧ after the editors' "leer".
Empty brackets [ ] stand before ⲙⲁϩⲉ.
The bracket opened at the line start closes after ⲙ̄; the sixth dot (x ≈ 657) is faint (below the detector's threshold) but clear at 6×.
The first dot (x ≈ 543) is faint (area 2) but clear at 6×. Seven letters of ⲡⲙⲁϩϥⲧⲁⲩ carry sublinear dots; under ϩ and ϥ the dot stands left of the descender.
Measured overline over ⲡⲛⲁ of [ⲡⲡⲛⲁ] (740–785): second ⲡ 84 %, ⲛ 100 %, ⲁ 58 %. Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (1237–1258): ⲙ 50 %, ⲛ 60 %. The bar over ⲛ of ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ (1158–1173) is a descender from l. 34.
